critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/app/routers/game.py:98-118 — /players/{player_id}/showcase endpoint is clean: 404 fail() on missing, reuses P.combat_profile + P.equipped_items + CS.resolved, exposes only public fields (hero.name/level, power breakdown, campaign region, castle_level, army_visual_tier, alliance tag/name, cosmetics, gear list without item_id/stats, domain_tiles count). is_me flag derived from principal → good for is_me client branching. No _id leakage, no private inventory/currencies exposed. Auth via current_user dependency → 401 automatic.

/app/frontend/app/player/[id].tsx — Single well-scoped file (~120 lines) with all showcase-* testIDs, animated Reanimated banner/lord entrances (banner scale/skew tilt from -8deg, lord translateY+opacity), correct route params via useLocalSearchParams, back/missing fallback with showcase-back-missing, conditional showcase-shop only when is_me, gear rendered as chips with slot+rarity+item_level. resolved cosmetics.army.color used for banner heraldic tint (falls back gracefully when null).

/app/frontend/app/alliance/index.tsx:72 — Pressable wrapper on the member Row uses full-width flex:1 and testID showcase-<player_id> — good touch target; caption 'tocca per la vetrina' is a nice affordance hint. Note: promote/kick buttons on the right (44px) don't overlap the showcase Pressable because they're siblings, not children — good.

/app/frontend/app/alliance/chat.tsx:74 — showcase-button inside moderation sheet correctly dismisses the sheet before router.push to avoid stale ref; uses object-form pathname/params which is more type-safe than string interpolation.
/app/frontend/app/alliance/boss.tsx:65 — hunter-<player_id> Pressable on each leaderboard row navigates via router.push to /player/[id]; simple and consistent with other entry points.
/app/frontend/app/profile.tsx:106 — my-showcase-button uses user?.player_id ?? '' which will route to /player/ if user is undefined, but PublicPlayer page guards with r.data or missing state → safe.

Nit (non-blocking): bot members in QATestf96c seed have no equipped_items and default hero.name='Lord' (no Sir/etc). This is a seeded-data property, not a bug — the endpoint correctly returns hero.name='Lord' when target.hero.name is falsy (fallback in game.py:110). If the PM wants richer bot showcases, seed_war_demo.py should populate bot hero names and equip a couple of gear pieces.
